runs.narrative: This commit does what it says: it removes the hardcoded dead Render.com API address from the authentication code (src/api/auth.ts) and instead pulls the shared API base URL from the app's central apiClient module, so all four login-related calls (sending an OTP code, verifying it for doctors, verifying it for patients, and refreshing an access token) now follow whatever address the demo startup script configures, which points at the cloudflared tunnel to the local backend. The diff matches every claim in the message, and the only other file touched is the project's routine session-tracking document, which was updated to hand the next step to a device tester. The code change looks complete and internally consistent, but the commit itself does not show that testing was done — its own notes say the fix still needs to be verified by running the demo and testing OTP login on a physical device, and it only states there are no new TypeScript errors. The pull request that later bundled this work describes it as device-verified, but that describes the merged state of the whole PR rather than this individual commit, so it is not a contradiction. This was attributed to story D1, and no story concerns arise. Marking it Code complete pending the on-device verification that the commit explicitly leaves outstanding. Follow-up for the developer: when/how will this be tested, and what's the ETA?

The change is small, self-contained, and internally consistent, and it is tied to story D1, which the commit message itself references. One caveat worth noting: the message states these calls now honor the environment variable set by the demo startup script, but this diff only shows the switch to the shared client value — the actual wiring of that client to the environment variable lives in another file that isn't part of this commit, so I can't confirm that end of the chain from what's here. This commit is attributed to story D1 and does exactly what its message describes: it removes the hardcoded dead Render.com address (`https://medrecord-api.onrender.com/v1`) from the app's authentication file and instead pulls the shared API address from the existing apiClient module, so all four login-related functions (send code, verify code, verify patient code, refresh token) now use whatever backend address the demo startup script sets, which is the live cloudflared tunnel. The code diff matches the claim cleanly and touches only that one source file plus a routine project-state tracking note; the tracking note itself is the normal kind of engineering log this repo carries and is not unrelated bundled content. The author states only that it is a one-line-style change with no new TypeScript errors, and the updated project notes explicitly route the next step to a device tester to confirm OTP login actually works on a phone, so on-device verification is still outstanding and I have not seen any evidence it was run; for that reason this is "Code complete" rather than "Tested." The merge PR #7 later claims the work was device-verified, but that describes the combined state of the whole PR at merge time and does not contradict this single commit being code-only at the point it was written. No story mismatch, no unexplained file deletions, and no other drift were found. Follow-up for the developer: when/how will this be tested, and what's the ETA?

This backend commit swaps the demo startup script from a Cloudflare (cloudflared) tunnel to a free, fixed ngrok web address so the local backend keeps the same URL every session. The diff supports the core claim: start-demo.sh now launches ngrok against the static domain, fails fast if that domain isn't configured, and has its wait/error handling rewritten to match; the file-ownership registry and the project status document are updated accordingly, and the tracking log records the session's steps. The commit message says the switch was checked end to end with curl (a command-line HTTP test) returning 200 OK once a special "skip browser warning" header is sent — I can't run anything myself, so I'm relying on the message and status doc, which describe a curl-level check rather than full in-app testing. The commit explicitly splits its work into a done part and an open part: the backend/script change is complete and curl-verified, but the matching frontend change (adding that header to src/api/apiClient.ts) is explicitly left queued for another agent, and the notes say on-device re-verification still needs to happen after that. Because the commit frames part of its own scope as still open, it is marked Pending. The PR-level "verified end-to-end on device" wording describes the whole merged PR, not this single commit, so it isn't treated as a conflict. No story or issue was attributed to this commit, and none is needed — it is a self-contained infrastructure and tooling change whose purpose is clear from the message and diff.

This commit adds a single HTTP header ("ngrok-skip-browser-warning: true") inside pinnedFetch, the one function that every API call in the app passes through, so the fix covers all callers at once rather than being repeated in each file. The purpose is to get past a browser-warning page that ngrok's free tunnel was serving instead of real data, an issue that had earlier been misdiagnosed as a network security failure. The code change in the diff matches what the message describes: the new header is applied on both the standard-fetch path and the certificate-pinned path. The developer states the fix was checked with a command-line request and a small Node script, and that no new TypeScript errors were introduced; I can see the code change but cannot independently confirm those test runs from the data given. The message is explicit that on-device testing through Expo Go has not happened yet and has been handed to a device tester, and because this is a transport-layer change that needs that confirmation, this is best treated as code-complete rather than tested. The other two changed files are routine internal tracking and session-status notes, not unrelated bundled content. No story or issue was attributed to this commit, and given that it is a self-contained infrastructure fix whose intent is clear on its own, none is needed here. Follow-up for the developer: when/how will this be tested, and what's the ETA?

This commit stands up a multi-phase hook-based governance system for the medrecord project: pre-tool gates that block work until a valid agent is declared, a file-ownership registry that limits which agent can edit which files, a workflow-sequencing gate that enforces a fix-and-retest loop when a testing agent reports defects, a session-start hook that injects current workflow state and fails closed if that state file is missing or corrupt, and a centralized trace-ID logger with a query script to reconstruct a feature's history. The diff is consistent with the commit message's description of cold-start hardening plus traceability, and the supporting state files (agent registry, ownership registry, workflow state, and an existing violation log) are included. No story or issue was attributed to this commit, and none is needed here: it is a self-contained infrastructure and governance change whose purpose is clear from its own contents. One item is worth a developer's eyes: the commit deletes the file .claude/hooks/check-agent-declared.sh entirely, but the commit message only frames the work as an addition and never mentions removing or replacing anything. The new agent-gate.sh looks like it supersedes the deleted script and the settings change swaps one for the other, so the removal may well be intentional, but it is not called out, which is a routine traceability gap. Separately, note that I only read the message and diff and did not run anything; the hooks themselves carry comments saying some enforcement paths are not yet verified or will not fire in the project's current one-session-per-agent model, so parts of this system are not confirmed working end to end.

This commit adds a small bootstrap exemption to one of the medrecord governance hook scripts (file-ownership-gate.sh) so that the first write which creates the session's agent-declaration marker file is allowed through, matching an exemption the sibling script (agent-gate.sh) already had; the stated problem is a cold-start deadlock where no session could ever declare an agent because the write that declares one required an agent to already be declared. The code change itself is small and consistent with that description, and the commit message says it was checked against a simulated cold start and against a Bash-redirect bypass path that stayed blocked, though I'm only reading the message and diff and can't independently confirm those checks were run. No story or issue was attributed to this commit, and none is really needed here since it is a self-contained infrastructure fix to the project's own tooling. The reason for flagging: the diff bundles clearly unrelated content types together — alongside the code fix and routine state-file updates, it adds linkedin-article-hook-governance-deadlock.md, which is a full publish-style write-up of the incident aimed at an outside audience rather than routine engineering documentation of the fix; this commit bundles unrelated content and should be split for traceability. Separately, the ownership registry file was reformatted in full and gained several new entries (for the article, an external failure-patterns file, and a /tmp/.medrecord_infra marker) that the commit message does not explain, which is worth a developer's eyes as a minor traceability gap.

This is the merge of PR #6, a batch of pre-pilot fixes for the MedRecord app, tied to story P3. The substantive code changes: the two patient screens P3 (Visit Record Detail) and P5 (Patient Profile) were switched from hardcoded mock data to real backend calls and their developer-only demo toggle buttons were removed; four cross-flow integration bugs were addressed (doctor-created patients can now log in, doctor-created visits appear in the patient timeline, patient consent data and revocations now propagate to the doctor side, and a crash in the Expo Go networking path was guarded); a new in-memory patient auth store was added; and the backend now rejects attempts to change a patient's mobile number on PATCH /patient/profile with a 400 error. The remainder of the diff is documentation and process files. One claim does not hold up: the commit and PR description say OTP resend with a 30-second cooldown was "added" to the doctor and patient login screens, but a resend-with-cooldown mechanism already existed in both screens and has been present since commit 12969c8; what this change actually does is lower the existing cooldown constant from 45 seconds to 30, not introduce the feature. That overstatement is why this is flagged for a developer to reword. Separately, I am only reading the diff and commit text here — the PR references device verification (4/4) and integration test runs (6/7) as passing, but I cannot confirm any testing from what is in front of me.

This commit touches a single file, the sync worker, and adds one piece of real behavior: if the network request for a queued item throws because the connection dropped, the code now waits about a second and a half and tries that request one more time before deciding the item failed. That part is self-contained and reads consistently. The problem is the commit message, which says "Fixed the sync bug, all edge cases handled now." The diff does not back up that claim in two ways. First, "the sync bug" is not identified anywhere and no story or issue was attributed to this commit, so it is not possible to tell from the message alone which bug was meant, though the change itself points clearly at dropped-connection retries during sync. Second, "all edge cases handled now" overstates what the code does: it adds exactly one retry for one failure mode, and the retry attempt itself is not wrapped in the same error handling, so if that second attempt also fails on a dropped connection the error would still go unhandled. There is also no mention in the message or the diff of any testing being run, so I cannot say this was verified. A developer should confirm which bug this targets and either narrow the message or add the handling needed to justify the "all edge cases" wording.

The commit message describes this as a performance-only refactor of the authorization middleware with "no behavioral change" and says all existing tests pass. The diff does not support that. It changes one condition in the access check from "and" to "or": previously a user was let through only if they were a doctor and the owner of the requested record, whereas now they are let through if they are either a doctor or the owner. That is a real change in behavior and it widens who can reach protected resources, which directly contradicts the "no behavioral change" wording and does not look like a performance change. The claim that all existing tests pass also is not evidenced here, since the diff touches only the middleware file and includes no test changes or test results for me to see. No story or issue was attributed to this commit, and none is strictly required to see the problem, but because the stated intent and the actual code disagree on something as sensitive as authorization, a developer should confirm whether the operator change is intentional and whether it was actually tested before this is treated as complete.
